title: A morphism from a separated algebraic space into a formal algebraic space is separated
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: For a morphism from a separated algebraic space U into a formal algebraic space X over a scheme, the lemma asserts that the morphism is separated (statement lines 3743-3748). The proof first notes that the statement makes sense because such a morphism is representable by algebraic spaces by an earlier result (proof lines 3750-3752). It then reduces the assertion to a base change: for a morphism from a scheme into the space one has to show that the base changed morphism is separated, and since the evident morphism from that base change to the base change of U over the scheme is a monomorphism, it suffices to show separatedness of the latter (proof lines 3752-3757). That morphism is a base change of the given separated morphism into the base scheme, so it is separated, and the argument closes (proof lines 3757-3759). The proof also lists the four general statements it uses, namely stability of separatedness under base change and under composition, and the facts that a monomorphism is separated and that separatedness of a morphism into the base follows from separatedness of the source (proof lines 3759-3763). The claim is H2: the reduction through a monomorphism to a base change of the given separated morphism is displayed and is the substance, and the general statements used are named rather than left implicit.
